title: 2025年12月四级真题 第2套 阅读2
paperTitle: 2025年12月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
passage:
P1 Adults dream during REM (rapid eye movement) sleep and infants have loads of REM. So, it might be fair to assume that babies have tons of dreams.

P2 But scientists believe REM serves a completely different purpose for newborns and infants than dreaming. When babies are in REM, it allows their brain to develop pathways, connections, and eventually, learn languages.

P3 Since your baby doesn't dream at this stage of brain development, it's safe to assume babies do not have nightmares, either. Nightmares stem from exposure to trauma(创伤), an overactive imagination, and the normal stresses of everyday life.

P4 Are you wondering, what do babies dream about? Good question, but the answer is nothing! So, when do babies start dreaming? The general consensus is that they start dreaming around the age of two. Psychologist David Foulkes studies children (from very small kids to teens) to bring the secrets of their dreams to the light of day. In his lab, he lets kids fall asleep and then wakes them 3 times a night and asks them to describe what they recall.

P5 Foulkes' findings are unsurprising. Basically, little kids have little dreams. But exactly what kids see while dreaming depends on their age. As children develop and grow, their dreams do too.

P6 Dreams of very small kids are usually just snapshots(快照), looking much more like a slideshow than a movie, when compared to the dreams of adults. They heavily feature animals and other familiar sights, like images of people eating. According to Foulkes, "Children's dream life…seems to be similar to their waking imagination and narration." Kids ages 5 – 9 begin seeing moving images and characters in action. Dreams now include multiple events strung together, one after the other. They also start developing greater ability to remember dreams. Still, that's not always the case: When roused during REM sleep, 25% of the kids in Foulkes' studies had no recollection of dreaming, a trend that continues through age 9.

P7 So, if your baby seems to be in a stressful state while sleeping or is upset upon waking, there may be other factors at play.

questions.q: What do scientists think of REM?
options: It is a sign of dreaming in adults and infants alike.
It is essential to human beings' language learning.
It determines the formation of connections in the brain.
It performs a different function in babies than in adults.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do scientists think of REM? 直接问科学家对 REM 的看法，是对原文具体观点的客 观转述。 51. What do scientists think of REM? A) It is a sign of dreaming in adults and infants alike. B) It is essential to human beings' language learning. C) It determines the formation of connections in the brain. D) It performs a different function in babies than in adults.

【拆句】Q51 结构是 "What do scientists think of REM?"，主谓宾极简，think of 在此意为 "对……的看法"，无陷阱。

【定位】But scientists believe REM serves a completely different purpose for newborns and infants than dreaming. 但科学家认为，对新生儿和婴儿而言，REM 所起的作用与做梦完全不同。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文明说婴儿在 REM 期"不做梦"，It is a sign of dreaming in adults and infants alike 反而说成人婴儿都做梦，与文意相反。 B) 以偏概全 原文 eventually, learn languages 只把语言学习列为大脑发育的一个结果，It is essential to human beings' language learning 把它拔高为 REM 的本质功能，范围 被放大。 C) 偷换概念 原文是 REM "allows" 婴儿大脑发育连接（提供条件），It determines the formation of connections in the brain 把 "提供条件" 偷换为 "决定"，强度被改。 D) ✓ 正确 a completely different purpose for newborns and infants than dreaming ↔ a different function in babies than in adults 预判 "REM 在婴儿与成人身上作用不同" 对应 It performs a different function in babies than in adults.，两端同义替换链完整。 从文章中我们可以推断出关于噩梦的什么信息? A) 它们常常发生在想象力活跃的人身上。 B) 它们发生在遭受情绪压力的人身上。 C) 它们在大脑发育的不同阶段各不相同。 D) 它们出现在成人和婴儿的睡眠中。

questions.q: What can we infer about nightmares from the passage?
options: They occur often in people with an active imagination.
They occur in people suffering from emotional stress.
They vary in different stages of brain development.
They appear in the sleep of both adults and infants.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can we infer about nightmares from the passage? 含 infer，属推断而非细节。

【拆句】Q52 主干 "What can we infer about nightmares"，about 引出推断对象，from the passage 是状语，结构简单。

【定位】Nightmares stem from exposure to trauma(创伤), an overactive imagination, and the normal stresses of everyday life. 噩梦源于创伤经历、过度活跃的想象，以及日常生活中的正常压力。 52. What can we infer about nightmares from the passage? A) They occur often in people with an active imagination. B) They occur in people suffering from emotional stress. C) They vary in different stages of brain development. D) They appear in the sleep of both adults and infants.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 P3 只把 an overactive imagination 列为三因之一，They occur often in people with an active imagination 把它单独抽出且加 often 强化，把一项当作主因。 B) ✓ 正确 the normal stresses of everyday life ↔emotional stress 预判 "承受情绪压力的人易做噩梦" 与 They occur in people suffering from emotional stress. 同义。 C) 无中生有 原文 P3 谈噩梦的成因，从未把噩梦与 "大脑发育阶段" 的关系作为话题；They vary in different stages of brain development 把别处的 brain development 概念硬套到 nightmares 上。 D) 与原文相反 原文 it's safe to assume babies do not have nightmares, either 明确婴儿不做噩 梦，They appear in the sleep of both adults and infants 反着说 "成人婴儿睡眠中都 出现"。 心理学家David Foulkes的研究目的是什么? A) 揭示儿童梦境的秘密。 B) 看儿童是否在两岁开始做梦。 C) 解决做梦与大脑发育之谜。 D) 证实关于儿童何时做梦的普遍共识。

questions.q: What is the aim of psychologist David Foulkes' study?
options: To reveal the secrets of children's dreams.
To see if children start dreaming at age two.
To solve the mystery of dreaming and brain growth.
To confirm the general consensus on when kids dream.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the aim of psychologist David Foulkes' study? 直接问研究目的，是对原文目的 句的客观转述。

【拆句】Q53 结构是 "What is the aim of psychologist David Foulkes' study?"，of 短语限定 aim，psychologist 是 David Foulkes 的同位身份说明，无陷阱。

【定位】Psychologist David Foulkes studies children (from very small kids to teens) to bring the secrets of their dreams to the light of day. 心理学家 David Foulkes 研究儿童（从年幼孩童到青少年），目的是把他们梦境的秘密揭示 于人前。 53. What is the aim of psychologist David Foulkes' study? A) To reveal the secrets of children's dreams. B) To see if children start dreaming at age two. C) To solve the mystery of dreaming and brain growth. D) To confirm the general consensus on when kids dream.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 to bring the secrets of their dreams to the light of day ↔ To reveal the secrets of children's dreams. 预判 "揭示儿童梦境秘密" 与 To reveal the secrets of children's dreams. 一一对应， 选 A。 B) 偷换概念 原文 they start dreaming around the age of two 是研究背景里的 "普遍共识"，并非 Foulkes 研究的目的；To see if children start dreaming at age two 把背景信息当成 研究目的。 C) 无中生有 原文未把 Foulkes 的目标说成 "解开做梦与大脑发育之谜"；To solve the mystery of dreaming and brain growth 引入了 P2 的 brain 概念硬接到 Foulkes 研究目的上。 D) 偷换概念 原文 The general consensus is that they start dreaming around the age of two. 表 示这是研究界已有共识，Foulkes 并非为证实它而研究；To confirm the general consensus on when kids dream 把 "已存在的共识" 当成 Foulkes 要证实的对象。 Foulkes关于儿童梦境的发现是什么? A) 它们以奇怪的动物为特征。 B) 它们对成人来说并不令人惊讶。 C) 它们随着年龄增长和演变。 D) 它们反映儿童的清醒生活。

questions.q: What are Foulkes' findings about kids' dreams?
options: They feature strange animals.
They are unsurprising to adults.
They grow and evolve with age.
They reflect kids' waking life.
questions.explain:
【判型】What are Foulkes' findings about kids' dreams? 直接问研究结论是什么，是细节题。

【拆句】Q54 结构是 "What are Foulkes' findings about kids' dreams?"，about kids' dreams 限定 findings 的范围，没有从句也没有否定，无陷阱。

【定位】Foulkes' findings are unsurprising. Basically, little kids have little dreams. But exactly what kids see while dreaming depends on their age. As children develop and grow, their dreams do too. Foulkes 的发现并不令人意外。本质上，小孩做的也是小梦。但孩子在梦中究竟看到什么， 取决于他们的年龄。随着孩子的发育成长，他们的梦也在发育成长。 54. What are Foulkes' findings about kids' dreams? A) They feature strange animals. B) They are unsurprising to adults. C) They grow and evolve with age. D) They reflect kids' waking life.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 They heavily feature animals and other familiar sights 只说幼儿梦多含动物等"熟悉 景象"，They feature strange animals 把动物拔成 "strange animals" 且当成所有孩子 梦的特征。 B) 答非所问 题问 findings 的内容；They are unsurprising to adults. 拿原文 "unsurprising" 的评 价词当做内容，Foulkes' findings are unsurprising 的 unsurprising 是对 "findings 本 身" 的评价，而非 findings 的实质内容。 C) ✓ 正确 As children develop and grow, their dreams do too ↔They grow and evolve with age. 预判 "梦随孩子发育而发育" 与 They grow and evolve with age. 完全对应，选 C。 D) 偷换概念 原文 Children's dream life…seems to be similar to their waking imagination and narration 的相似对象是 "清醒时的想象与叙事"，They reflect kids' waking life. 把 "想 象/叙事" 偷换成 "waking life"（清醒生活本身）。 关于醒来时看起来心烦意乱的婴儿,我们可以假设什么? A) 他们违背自己的意愿被唤醒了。 B) 他们被噩梦打扰了。 C) 他们难以回忆梦境的画面。 D) 他们受到了做梦以外的其他事物的影响。

questions.q: What can we assume about babies who appear upset upon waking?
options: They have been roused against their will.
They have been disturbed by a nightmare.
They have trouble recollecting the images of their dreams.
They have been affected by something other than dreaming.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can we assume about babies who appear upset upon waking? 含 assume，按 推断题处理。

【拆句】Q55 结构是 "What can we assume about babies who appear upset upon waking?"， who 引导定语从句修饰 babies，upon waking 是时间状语 "一醒来时"，整句无否定无比 较，理解关键是把 who 从句翻成 "那些一醒来就显得不安的婴儿"。

【定位】So, if your baby seems to be in a stressful state while sleeping or is upset upon waking, there may be other factors at play. 因此，如果你的婴儿睡觉时显得紧张、或一醒来就不安，那很可能是别的因素在起作用。 55. What can we assume about babies who appear upset upon waking? A) They have been roused against their will. B) They have been disturbed by a nightmare. C) They have trouble recollecting the images of their dreams. D) They have been affected by something other than dreaming.

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文 P7 没有说婴儿被人弄醒；They have been roused against their will. 凭空添加 "被弄醒" + "违背意愿" 两个文本无据的语义。 B) 与原文相反 原文 babies do not have nightmares 明确说婴儿不做噩梦；They have been disturbed by a nightmare. 反着说婴儿被噩梦惊扰。 C) 答非所问 题问 "哭醒原因"，They have trouble recollecting the images of their dreams. 把焦 点换成 "回忆梦境困难"，且 25% of the kids in Foulkes' studies had no recollection of dreaming 说的是 5-9 岁孩子，而非 "babies"。 D) ✓ 正确 there may be other factors at play ↔ They have been affected by something other than dreaming. 预判 "原因不是做梦" 与 They have been affected by something other than dreaming. 完全对应，选 D。
